plan.title: Confounded lung treated vs control DE + enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 lung RNA-seq samples (6 treated, 6 control) come from salmon gene-level counts with batch B2 holding all treated and B1 holding all controls — batch is perfectly confounded with condition. This makes 'batch effect' and 'condition effect' mathematically inseparable: no design can distinguish them. Per DESeq2/knowledge-base consensus (R-0005), we do NOT fit a batch term, do NOT run ComBat-seq/removeBatchEffect/SVA (any of these would strip the condition signal along with the batch, or fail because the model matrix is not full rank). Instead: (1) QC first to show the batch/condition split visually (PCA, sample-distance heatmap) so the confound is documented, not hidden; (2) minimal low-count pre-filter; (3) DESeq2 Wald test with design ~condition only, explicit reference level (control), apeglm-shrunken LFCs; (4) BH-FDR at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering; (5) every output gene/pathway explicitly labeled 'condition and batch confounded — cannot attribute to treatment alone'; (6) GO/Hallmark/Reactome/WikiPathways over-representation on the significant gene list (fallback from ranked GSEA per the knowledge-service's binding rule for this exact confounded-batch situation) with the tested genes as universe; (7) a report that states the confound as the central caveat rather than a footnote. The research question ('which genes differ between treated and control') is answerable only as 'which genes differ between B2/treated and B1/control' — the two are indistinguishable here, and the report must say so plainly rather than imply causal attribution to treatment.
